title: Geometric stalks commute with tensor products and scalar extension on the etale site
statement:
Let $Y$ be a scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] with a geometric point $\bar y$, stalks at $\bar y$ being those of [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], and let $Y_{\Et}$ be its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. For a ring $R$, a sheaf of left $R$-modules on $Y_{\Et}$ is a sheaf of abelian groups with a left $R$-module structure on every group of sections for which all restriction maps are $R$-linear; sheafification of presheaves of $R$-modules is that of [def-weil-pbc-sheafification].

1. *(Tensor products.)* Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring and $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules on $Y_{\Et}$. Let $\mathcal F\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal G$ be the sheafification of the presheaf $U\mapsto\mathcal F(U)\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal G(U)$, and for $s\in\mathcal F(U)$, $t\in\mathcal G(U)$ write $s\otimes t$ for the image of $s\otimes t$ in $(\mathcal F\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal G)(U)$. Then there is a unique $\Lambda$-linear map $\mathcal F_{\bar y}\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal G_{\bar y}\to(\mathcal F\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal G)_{\bar y}$ with $s_{\bar y}\otimes t_{\bar y}\mapsto(s\otimes t)_{\bar y}$, and it is an isomorphism, natural in $\mathcal F$ and $\mathcal G$ and compatible with the associativity, commutativity and unit ($\underline\Lambda\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal F\cong\mathcal F$, with $\underline\Lambda$ the constant sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]) isomorphisms on both sides.
2. *(Scalar extension.)* Let $\Lambda\to\Lambda'$ be a homomorphism of rings, not necessarily commutative, so that $\Lambda'$ is a $(\Lambda',\Lambda)$-bimodule, and let $\mathcal F$ be a sheaf of left $\Lambda$-modules on $Y_{\Et}$. Let $\Lambda'\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal F$ be the sheafification of the presheaf of left $\Lambda'$-modules $U\mapsto\Lambda'\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal F(U)$, and write $\lambda'\otimes s$ for the image of $\lambda'\otimes s$ in $(\Lambda'\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal F)(U)$. Then there is a unique $\Lambda'$-linear map $\Lambda'\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal F_{\bar y}\to(\Lambda'\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal F)_{\bar y}$ with $\lambda'\otimes s_{\bar y}\mapsto(\lambda'\otimes s)_{\bar y}$, and it is an isomorphism of left $\Lambda'$-modules, natural in $\mathcal F$; for homomorphisms $\Lambda\to\Lambda'\to\Lambda''$ it is compatible with the identifications $\Lambda''\otimes_{\Lambda'}(\Lambda'\otimes_\Lambda-)\cong\Lambda''\otimes_\Lambda-$ on stalks and on sheaves.

proof.text: Use Mathlib Point.sheafFiber.Monoidal and its monoidal sheafification comparison. The private stalk_tensorator calculation identifies its tensorator with the presheaf fiber tensorator followed by the fiber of the lax tensor map of sheafToPresheaf: apply NatTrans.IsMonoidal.tensor to presheafToSheafCompSheafFiberIso.inv, expand the right-adjoint tensor map, use the sheafification triangle identity, and cancel the sheafification tensorator and its inverse.

Mathlib tensorHom_comp_toPresheafFiber_mu and toPresheafFiber_naturality give the pure-germ formula for that tensorator. It is an isomorphism by the strong monoidal instance. The opposite category of pointed neighborhoods is filtered; the tensor of the two presheaf fiber colimit cocones is therefore colimiting (IsColimit.tensor). Its hom_ext proves uniqueness from the formula on common-neighborhood tensor coprojections.

Naturality is Functor.LaxMonoidal.mu_natural. The constant-unit equality is definitional, and associativity and both unit diagrams are the lax monoidal axioms. For symmetry, use the same tensor-colimit hom_ext, move the module braiding past the tensor coprojections, use the pure-germ formula and fiber naturality, and finish with the lax braided axiom of sheafToPresheaf.

For arbitrary rings the existing ringExtendScalars and ringExtendScalarsAdj give a scalar extension functor and its adjunction. For any supplied scalar-extension adjunction E left adjoint to restriction, E preserves colimits. Compose the inverses of presheafFiberCompIso E and presheafToSheafCompSheafFiberIso. The coprojection formula of the first and naturality of the sheafification unit identify its action on E of a germ. Unit naturality transposes this into the required 1-tensor germ equation. Transpose any two candidate maps through adj.homEquiv and apply presheafFiber_hom_ext to prove component uniqueness. Both factors are isomorphisms. Whisker the two comparison natural isomorphisms to obtain the natural transformation, and component uniqueness proves its uniqueness and the isomorphism claim for every candidate.

For successive extensions let k be sheafification of the presheaf map E23(toSheafify(F composed with E12)). Since E23 is a left adjoint it preserves sheafification-inverting maps, so k is an isomorphism. Compose k inverse with sheafification of F whiskered with the canonical leftAdjointUniq isomorphism a to construct b. Naturality of toSheafify and cancellation of k prove the required section equation. Map the presheaf fiber colimit cocone of F through E12 composed with E23 and use its hom_ext. On a coprojection, the three scalar comparison coprojection formulas, the section equation for b, and naturality of a identify the two composites.
